ai.description: Subansiri’s Tree Frog is a medium-sized rhacophorid. It features a pale brown dorsum with dark brown markings, a white belly, and distinct dark horizontal bars on its hind limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates subansiriensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark brown, hourglass-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates subansiriensis* inhabits subtropical broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 200 and 500 meters above sea level.
ai.behavior: *Polypedates subansiriensis* is primarily nocturnal, exhibiting specialized arboreal behavior by foraging for small insects among vegetation near forest streams at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates subansiriensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies. Clutch size is typically 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates subansiriensis* is endemic to Arunachal Pradesh, India, specifically inhabiting the Subansiri River basin at elevations between 200 and 500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Polypedates subansiriensis* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams.
